sources.citation: Jacquesson, François. 2015. Persons and Grammar in Meyor (author preprint, HAL halshs-01672242, submitted 23 Dec 2017).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Same content as the published chapter: Netan-pu 'is indeed the only one to have tones' (preprint p. 1, fn 4); dialects differ 'in prosody, lexicon, and grammar'. Nothing on stress placement.

sources.citation: Jacquesson, François. 2015. Persons and grammar in Meyor. In Mark W. Post, Stephen Morey & Scott DeLancey (eds.), Language and Culture in Northeast India and Beyond: In Honor of Robbins Burling, 100-113. Canberra: Asia-Pacific Linguistics (A-PL 023). Handle 1885/38458.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology section and nothing on word stress. p. 101: of the three Indian-side dialects (Kaho, Walong, Netan-pu) the Netan-pu variety is 'reputed for its tunes, maybe the only one to have tones'; the dialects 'have differences in prosody, lexicon, and grammar'. fn 5: 'among Meyor where tones are the privilege of the Netan-pu'. Data are Kaho dialect. Later uses of 'stress' (pp. 101, 105, 108) mean emphasis/focus, not word accent.
